claims.explanation: PP-2 is a Src-family kinase inhibitor, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on Src/FAK signaling for survival, which is enhanced by EGFR activation and by loss of negative regulators such as PTEN. Lines with activating EGFR mutations or PTEN loss are enriched among sensitive lines, whereas RAS/BRAF-mutant lines with intact RTK-independent growth are relatively protected.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006) are among the most killed; EGFR signaling activates Src/FAK
PTEN loss in sensitive lines (HEC265, KALS1) may increase PI3K/Src-dependent survival signaling
Higher Src expression/activity would increase dependence on the drug's primary target
FAK (PTK2) is activated downstream of Src and mediates survival signaling; high FAK may indicate Src-pathway dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (UACC62, K029AX, LOXIMVI) are among the least affected, suggesting MAPK-driven survival bypasses Src
NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, KU1919) are less affected, consistent with RAS-driven Src independence
KRAS-mutant lines appear in both groups but several KRAS-mutant lines are least affected, suggesting RAS activation reduces Src dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is enriched in less-affected lines (BICR6, FTC133, LOXIMVI)
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among the least affected, consistent with MAPK pathway activation bypassing Src
MET-mutant HGC27 is least affected, suggesting RTK bypass of Src inhibition
KIT-mutant KYSE510 is least affected, suggesting alternative RTK survival signaling
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines but also common in resistant lines, so this is weak evidence
